notes:
Account snapshot:
- Prospect: Nimbus Uptime Labs — edge orchestration + high-availability inference for telco and logistics customers. Heavy real-time inference (sub-40ms p95 target for chat routing) and batch embedding pipelines for nightly indexing.
- Primary ask: dedicated GPU pool with explicit throughput guarantees and an SLA that matches their contract commitments to end customers. They want defined credit schedule if SLOs missed, plus predictable maintenance windows.
- Key quote from CTO (2/18 call): "We cannot abdicate availability to bursty shared tenants — need predictable tails and credits that scale to the business impact."
SLA topics in negotiation (current):
1) Uptime target: legal pushing for 99.99% (≈52 minutes downtime/year). Redwood proposed 99.95% for Dedicated with escalation path to private on-prem option for critical workloads.
2) Credit schedule: Redwood standard credits tiered by outage duration; Nimbus demands monetary offset capped at 30% ARR for repeated incidents. Discussed adding 10% service credit per major incident after three incidents in 12 months, not to exceed X. Legal to define exact cap.
3) Maintenance windows: Nimbus wants 1x/month rolling maintenance with 00:00–04:00 local window and pre-notice 7 days. Redwood prefers quarterly major windows + weekly micro-patches with 48-hour notice. Need compromise on frequency vs. SLA carveouts.
4) Support & response times: requirement is 15 min P1 response, 2-hour P1 remediation SLA for infra-level incidents. Redwood proposed 30-min response / 4-hour remediation for Dedicated; pushing to include prioritized SE on-call during business hours.
5) Reserved GPU planning: capacity planning doc shared (drive link). Nimbus expects guaranteed baseline of 48 A100-equivalent slots, with automated burst to 80 for 30% higher traffic days. Discussed commitment tiers and overage pricing.
6) Throughput & latency SLOs: target p95 latency <=40ms for chat path, p99 <=120ms for small-context reranking (<=512 tokens). Throughput targeted at 500 qps sustained across region with ability to scale to 1.2k qps for peak windows. Tests scheduled.
POC & evaluation notes:
- POC started 2026-01-12: initial canary on Redwood Dedicated (8 GPUs) for backend reranking.
- Load test plan: two-phase — synthetic traffic (Mar 2026 week 2) then production shadowing (Mar 2026 week 4). SE to instrument latency histograms and tail analysis.
- Security review: completed SOC2 + KMS integration checklist pending. Data residency box: need EU-only partitioning for EU customers.
- Pricing: CFO wants line-item for dedicated reservation + on-prem hardware transfer (if needed). Expected ARR band discussed.
CRM shorthand / next items:
- Legal follow-up: send redlines to Nimbus counsel by 2026-03-20.
- Engineering: confirm sustained 500 qps with <40ms p95 on test harness by 2026-03-18.
- Ops: draft escalation runbook + contact list; provide 24/7 on-call add-on pricing.
- Procurement: receive final PO by 2026-04-15 to hit May go-live.
Concerns and risk points:
- Nimbus insists on 99.99% at enterprise price — will create revenue pushback and potential to require private deployment for their top-tier tenants.
- Credit schedule negotiation likely biggest gate for procurement committee.
- On-prem packaging cost unknown; procurement wants cost waterfall.
